# Synchronicity

Synchronicity takes the coincidence of events in space and time as meaning something more than mere chance, namely, a peculiar interdependence of objective events among themselves as well as with the subjective states of the observer or observers. I chose this term because the simultaneous occurrence of two meaningful but not causally connected events seemed to me an essential criterion.

By synchronicity I mean the occurrence of a meaningful coincidence in time. It can take three forms: the coincidence of a certain psychic content with a corresponding objective process which is perceived to take place simultaneously; the coincidence of a subjective psychic state with a phantasm (dream or vision) which later turns out to be a more or less faithful reflection of a simultaneous objective event; or the same, except that the event perceived takes place in the future.

The psychoid nature of the archetype contains much that throws light on the nature of synchronicity. The archetype represents psychic probability, portraying ordinary instinctual events in the form of types. It is a special psychic instance of the general physical concept of the connection through acausal orderedness. The meaningful connection between causally unrelated events points to a unitary aspect of existence that transcends our customary categories of space, time, and causation.

What I found were coincidences which were connected so meaningfully that their chance concurrence would represent a degree of improbability that would have to be expressed by an astronomical figure. In view of the difficulty of the problem, I do not think I could have done better than to collect, classify, and describe the phenomenon of synchronicity.
